advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the specific InvalidLabelError message/branch per bad input in test_sanitize_label_raises_on_every_rejection_reason so a collapsed guard cannot pass on the wrong reason.
evidence: source raises the more specific InvalidLabelError with a distinct message per branch: jira_fields.py:113 'Label is empty after strip', jira_fields.py:115 'internal whitespace', jira_fields.py:119 'comma', jira_fields.py:121 'exceeds ... limit'
test only asserts `with pytest.raises(ValueError):` (line 232), matching on the base class without discriminating the reason
advisory.finding: The 'raises on every rejection reason' label test asserts only bare ValueError across four distinct bad inputs in one loop, so it does not verify each input trips its OWN rejection branch — an extraction that collapsed two guards (e.g. whitespace input caught by the empty-after-strip check) could still pass on the wrong reason while the test name implies each reason is independently pinned.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use pytest.raises(ValueError, match=...) with a per-input expected substring (e.g. 'whitespace', 'comma', 'empty after strip', 'exceeds'), iterating over (input, expected_match) pairs.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the module docstring to note the added acb2 oracles pin module-internal outputs directly (not only JiraBackend delegation).
evidence: docstring: 'Byte-for-byte pins on the CURRENT outputs of the pure Jira mappers/sanitizers, asserting that ``JiraBackend``'s role Protocols delegate to them'

new tests import module internals directly, not through the backend: line 288 'from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira.probe import classify_probe_response', line 333 'from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira.jira_fields import _RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK', line 358 'from rebar_reconciler.link_direction import resolve_inbound_link'
advisory.finding: The module docstring (lines 1-12) still scopes the file as S2/bbf1 byte-for-byte pins on JiraBackend DELEGATION, but the new acb2 block reaches past the backend directly into module internals (classify_probe_response, _RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK, resolve_inbound_link) that are not accessed via a JiraBackend role Protocol, so the header no longer accurately describes the file's contents.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a pin for status 'deleted' -> 'Done' in test_map_fields_to_remote_maps_every_status_plus_unmapped_default so a dropped/renamed 'deleted' map entry turns the oracle RED.
evidence: Test loop pins only idea/open/in_progress/closed/blocked/cancelled: `for local_status, jira_state in { "idea": "IDEA", "open": "To Do", "in_progress": "In Progress", "closed": "Done", "blocked": "In Progress", "cancelled": "Done", }.items():` (test_backend_characterization.py:138-145) and comment `# The default branch an extraction is most likely to drop.` (line 147)

Source map has the extra key: `"closed": "Done", "cancelled": "Done", "deleted": "Done",` in outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:101-103)

map_fields_to_remote routes status via `out["status"] = outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS.get(value, "To Do")` (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/backend.py:84), so a dropped 'deleted' key silently becomes 'To Do' with no failing assertion
`search_files 'deleted'` over the test file returns no matches — 'deleted' is unpinned
ticket fe15-3bc4-ed70-4b61 confirms 'deleted' is a real TicketStatus (src/rebar/types.py:21) and that the drift between the two status-map copies is real and reachable
advisory.finding: The 'every status' pin for map_fields_to_remote omits the 'deleted' key, which outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS maps to 'Done'; because unmapped statuses fall through to the 'To Do' default, an extraction that drops the 'deleted' entry would silently change deleted->Done into deleted->To Do and this suite would still pass — a regression-blind spot in the exact map the oracle claims to freeze.
scenarios: J2 extraction consolidates or relocates _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS and drops/renames the 'deleted' key; deleted->Done silently becomes deleted->To Do and CI stays green
A future edit removes the 'deleted' entry as apparently-dead code; the byte-for-byte oracle fails to fire
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `"deleted": "Done",` to the status dict in test_map_fields_to_remote_maps_every_status_plus_unmapped_default (and, for symmetry with the source, note that outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS carries 'deleted' while jira_fields._LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA does not, per fe15).
